[SYSTEM] You are a Python ML engineer. Write a single, self-contained Python script that trains and evaluates the architecture from the proposal for the BirdCLEF 2026 multi-label task. ## Input tensor shape — READ THIS FIRST The data loader produces tensors of shape **(batch, 1, n_mels, time_frames)** — a 4-dimensional tensor, image-like. Typical values: (32, 1, 128, 313). This means: - Use `nn.Conv2d`, NOT `nn.Conv1d`. Conv1d only accepts 3D tensors (batch, channels, time) and will crash on 4D input. - Use `nn.MaxPool2d` / `nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d`, not the 1D versions. - Treat each spectrogram as an image with 1 channel. ## Channel tracking in stacked Conv2d layers The FIRST Conv2d must have `in_channels=1` because the input has 1 channel. Every subsequent Conv2d's `in_channels` MUST equal the previous Conv2d's `out_channels`. A common LLM mistake is: self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(1, 64, 3) # out: 64 self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(1, 64, 3) # WRONG: expects 1 channel, gets 64 The correct version: self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(1, 64, 3) # out: 64 self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(64, 128, 3) # in=64 matches conv1 out=64 Before writing each Conv2d, think about what tensor flows into it and explicitly set `in_channels` to the previous layer's `out_channels`. If you are unsure, use `nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d((1, 1))` to collapse the spatial dims and a `nn.Linear(out_channels, num_classes)` at the end — that guarantees the output dimension is correct regardless of input size. ## Architecture sources — TWO valid paths The proposal's `architecture` field tells you what to build: (A) REGISTRY MODEL — the `architecture` value matches a name in the Model Registry (e.g. "cnn_small_v1", "efficientnet_b0"): → Copy the registry's `import_snippet` VERBATIM. Use the EXACT capitalization shown there (e.g. `CnnSmallV1`, NOT `cnn_small_v1`). → Registry models are in `pipelines.models` or in `torchvision.models`. The snippet tells you which. Do NOT invent imports like `from torchvision.models import CnnSmallV1` — that is wrong; CnnSmallV1 lives in `pipelines.models`. (B) CUSTOM MODEL — the `architecture` describes a free-form design that is not a registry name (e.g. "ResNet-style 4-block CNN with SE attention"): → Define the full `nn.Module` class(es) inline. Everything must be imported from `torch`, `torch.nn`, `torchvision`, `torchaudio`, `sklearn`, `numpy`, or `pipelines`, OR defined within the script. → The final logit vector MUST have length 234 (multi-label output). → If your custom model USES a registry model as a backbone or sub- component (e.g. `self.backbone = CnnSmallV1(...)`), you MUST import it at the TOP of the file: from pipelines.models import CnnSmallV1 Imports inside class definitions do NOT work — Python resolves the name when the __init__ runs, not when the class is defined. ## Hard requirements (apply to BOTH paths) - Write code at MODULE scope, not inside a main() function. The script is executed top-to-bottom as a standalone Python file. - `import torch` at the top. Also import `torch.nn as nn`, `numpy as np`, `json`, `os`, and `time` — you will need all of them. - The training device is read from the `BIRDCLEF_DEVICE` env var. Do this at the top of the script, right after imports: DEVICE_NAME = os.environ.get("BIRDCLEF_DEVICE", "cpu") device = torch.device(DEVICE_NAME) print(f"device: {device}", flush=True) Do NOT hardcode "cpu" / "mps" / "cuda" anywhere. Do NOT call `torch.cuda.is_available()` or `torch.backends.mps.is_available()` — the orchestrator has already resolved which device to use. Just trust the env var. ALL tensors AND the model must live on this device: - `model = MyModel(...).to(device)` right after instantiation. - Inside the training loop, move each batch: `x, y = x.to(device), y.to(device)` - Before handing predictions to sklearn for metrics, move them back to CPU: `probs = torch.sigmoid(model(x)).cpu().numpy()`. Stick to `torch.float32` (the default). MPS has limited `float64` support — do NOT call `.double()` or set `dtype=torch.float64`. - Use the fixed data loader. DO NOT pass any path arguments — it reads them from environment variables set by the sandbox. ALSO DO NOT pass `batch_size`, `num_workers`, `persistent_workers` or `prefetch_factor`: these are configured once for the whole project in `config/config.yaml` under the `training:` section and flow into the sandbox via BIRDCLEF_* env vars. The data loader reads them automatically. Just do: from pipelines.data_loader import load_precomputed_dataset train_loader, val_loader, num_classes = load_precomputed_dataset( augmentation={"time_shift": True, "noise_injection": True}, ) If a specific experiment genuinely needs to override one of these (e.g. a very memory-hungry model that can't use the configured batch_size), you may pass that one argument explicitly — everything else still falls back to the config. - CPU thread saturation (only matters when DEVICE_NAME == "cpu", harmless otherwise): right after `import torch`, set the thread count explicitly so PyTorch uses every available core for data-loader augmentation and any CPU fallback ops: torch.set_num_threads(os.cpu_count() or 4) The executor also sets OMP_NUM_THREADS via the subprocess env, but calling torch.set_num_threads is the belt-and-suspenders guarantee. - Multi-label loss: `nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss()`. The model must output raw logits of shape `(batch, num_classes)`. Apply `torch.sigmoid` only when computing metrics. - Metric: macro-averaged ROC-AUC over classes that have at least one positive label. Use `sklearn.metrics.roc_auc_score` per column and take the mean. Skip columns with no positives to avoid the sklearn error. - HARD CAP: `EPOCHS = 1`. Always. No exceptions. Write literally `EPOCHS = 1` in your code. Do NOT copy the proposed epochs value, do NOT use max(1, ...) or anything fancy. Just `EPOCHS = 1`. We are in fast-iteration mode — longer training is not what we want right now. Any code with `EPOCHS > 1` will be rejected. - At the VERY END of the script, write `results.json` in the CURRENT directory. This file is the single source of truth for the agent — if you don't write it, the experiment counts as failed. Schema: {"metrics": {"roc_auc_macro": , "loss": }, "training_curves": {"loss": [...], "roc_auc_macro": [...]}, "duration_seconds": } If training fails, still write `results.json` with an `error` key: {"error": ""} - Do NOT import: subprocess, urllib, requests, socket. - Do NOT call `os.system(...)`, `eval(...)`, `exec(...)`, or `__import__`. - Do NOT download anything from the internet. - Do NOT write files outside the current directory. ## Progress logging — IMPORTANT The agent operator is watching the live terminal output to see whether the training is progressing or hung. A silent script makes this impossible. You MUST include the following `print(..., flush=True)` calls so the operator can see progress in real time: - Before loading data: "loading data..." - After load_precomputed_dataset: "data loaded: classes, train, val" - After model instantiation: "model built:

parameters" - At the start of each epoch: "epoch / starting..." - Every ~10% of train batches: " epoch [%] batch / loss=" - Before validation: "epoch : running validation..." - At the end of each epoch: "epoch / done: loss= roc_auc_macro=" - On final completion: "all done: final roc_auc_macro=" - On exception (inside except): "training failed: : " ALWAYS pass `flush=True` to print() — without it, the output is block- buffered and the operator sees nothing for minutes at a time. ## Common PyTorch pitfalls that have crashed previous runs ### 1. `self.relu` vs `F.relu` — do NOT mix them up There are two correct ways to apply ReLU (or any other activation) in a PyTorch nn.Module. You must pick ONE per module and stick to it. WRONG (this is the #1 cause of AttributeError failures in our runs): class MyModel(nn.Module): def __init__(self, num_classes): super().__init__() self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(1, 32, 3, padding=1) # forgot to define self.relu here! def forward(self, x): x = self.relu(self.conv1(x)) # AttributeError: no attribute 'relu' CORRECT option A — register the activation as a submodule: class MyModel(nn.Module): def __init__(self, num_classes): super().__init__() self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(1, 32, 3, padding=1) self.relu = nn.ReLU(inplace=True) # <-- defined in __init__ def forward(self, x): x = self.relu(self.conv1(x)) # works CORRECT option B — use the functional form (simpler, no __init__ line): import torch.nn.functional as F class MyModel(nn.Module): def __init__(self, num_classes): super().__init__() self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(1, 32, 3, padding=1) def forward(self, x): x = F.relu(self.conv1(x)) # works, no self.relu needed Rule of thumb: option B (`F.relu`) is simpler for stateless activations (relu, gelu, sigmoid, softmax). Use it unless you have a specific reason to need option A. Same applies to `F.max_pool2d`, `F.adaptive_avg_pool2d`, `F.dropout`, etc. ### 2. Shape mismatch on the flatten → linear boundary A classic bug: after a stack of Conv2d + pooling, the spatial size of the feature map depends on the input. Writing `nn.Linear(2048, num_classes)` only works if the feature map's flattened size is exactly 2048. Change the input shape and it crashes with: RuntimeError: mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (32x1600 and 2048x234) FIX: always end your Conv stack with `nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d((1, 1))` before flattening. That guarantees a (batch, C, 1, 1) → (batch, C) tensor regardless of the input spatial size. Then `nn.Linear(C, num_classes)` where C is the out_channels of the last Conv2d. Example: self.features = nn.Sequential( nn.Conv2d(1, 32, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(32), nn.ReLU(inplace=True), nn.MaxPool2d(2), nn.Conv2d(32, 64, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(64), nn.ReLU(inplace=True), nn.MaxPool2d(2), nn.Conv2d(64, 128, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(128), nn.ReLU(inplace=True), ) self.pool = nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d((1, 1)) # → (batch, 128, 1, 1) self.head = nn.Linear(128, num_classes) # in_features = 128 (last conv out_channels) def forward(self, x): x = self.features(x) x = self.pool(x).flatten(1) # → (batch, 128) return self.head(x) The `.flatten(1)` collapses dimensions 1+ into one, so (batch, 128, 1, 1) → (batch, 128). No shape arithmetic, no crashes. ### 3. Channel tracking in stacked Conv2d (already covered above) Each Conv2d's `in_channels` MUST equal the previous Conv2d's `out_channels`. See the "Channel tracking in stacked Conv2d layers" section. ## Variable scoping reminder Define `num_classes` at module scope — it comes from load_precomputed_dataset and you will use it to instantiate the model. Do NOT put it inside a function and then try to use it from the outside — that causes NameError. Likewise, do NOT build a `hyperparams` dict and then look things up from it (`hyperparams["augmentation"]`) — just use the values directly. import json
import os
import time
import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score
from pipelines.data_loader import load_precomputed_dataset
from pipelines.models import CnnSmallV1

DEVICE_NAME = os.environ.get("BIRDCLEF_DEVICE", "cpu")
device = torch.device(DEVICE_NAME)
print(f"device: {device}", flush=True)
if DEVICE_NAME == "cpu":
    torch.set_num_threads(os.cpu_count() or 4)

EPOCHS = 1
LR = 0.001

start = time.time()
results = {}
try:
    print("loading data...", flush=True)
    train_loader, val_loader, num_classes = load_precomputed_dataset(
        augmentation={"time_shift": True, "noise_injection": True},
    )
    print(
        f"data loaded: {num_classes} classes, "
        f"{len(train_loader.dataset)} train samples, "
        f"{len(val_loader.dataset)} val samples",
        flush=True,
    )

    model = CnnSmallV1(num_classes=num_classes, in_channels=1)
    model = model.to(device)
    n_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())
    print(f"model built: {n_params:,} parameters", flush=True)

    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=LR)
    criterion = nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss()

    n_train_batches = len(train_loader)
    log_every = max(1, n_train_batches // 10)

    curves = {"loss": [], "roc_auc_macro": []}
    for epoch in range(EPOCHS):
        print(
            f"epoch {epoch + 1}/{EPOCHS} starting "
            f"({n_train_batches} batches)...",
            flush=True,
        )
        model.train()
        epoch_losses = []
        for batch_idx, (x, y) in enumerate(train_loader):
            x = x.to(device, dtype=torch.float32, non_blocking=True)
            y = y.to(device, dtype=torch.float32, non_blocking=True)
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            logits = model(x)
            loss = criterion(logits, y)
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            epoch_losses.append(float(loss.item()))

            if (batch_idx + 1) % log_every == 0 or batch_idx + 1 == n_train_batches:
                pct = 100.0 * (batch_idx + 1) / n_train_batches
                print(
                    f"  epoch {epoch + 1} [{pct:5.1f}%] "
                    f"batch {batch_idx + 1}/{n_train_batches} "
                    f"loss={loss.item():.4f}",
                    flush=True,
                )

        print(f"epoch {epoch + 1}: running validation...", flush=True)
        model.eval()
        all_probs, all_targs = [], []
        with torch.no_grad():
            for x, y in val_loader:
                x = x.to(device, dtype=torch.float32, non_blocking=True)
                all_probs.append(torch.sigmoid(model(x)).cpu().numpy())
                all_targs.append(y.numpy())
        probs = np.concatenate(all_probs, axis=0)
        targs = np.concatenate(all_targs, axis=0)

        aucs = []
        for c in range(targs.shape[1]):
            if targs[:, c].sum() > 0:
                aucs.append(roc_auc_score(targs[:, c], probs[:, c]))
        val_auc = float(np.mean(aucs)) if aucs else 0.0
        epoch_loss = float(np.mean(epoch_losses))

        curves["loss"].append(epoch_loss)
        curves["roc_auc_macro"].append(val_auc)
        print(
            f"epoch {epoch + 1}/{EPOCHS} done: "
            f"loss={epoch_loss:.4f} roc_auc_macro={val_auc:.4f}",
            flush=True,
        )

    results = {
        "metrics": {
            "roc_auc_macro": curves["roc_auc_macro"][-1],
            "loss": curves["loss"][-1],
        },
        "training_curves": curves,
        "duration_seconds": time.time() - start,
    }
    print(f"all done: final roc_auc_macro={curves['roc_auc_macro'][-1]:.4f}", flush=True)
except Exception as exc:
    results = {"error": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"}
    print(f"training failed: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", flush=True)

with open("results.json", "w") as fh:
    json.dump(results, fh)
